properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued September 16 at 2:15AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
A Marine Weather Statement has been issued for the following areas...
Volusia-Brevard County Line to Sebastian Inlet 0-20 nm...

At 213 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated gusty showers and possibly a
thunderstorm, capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. This
convection was located offshore Brevard county, in particular 10 nm
east of Indialantic, moving west at 20 knots. These showers will
produce brief downpours and gusty winds as they push onshore and
across the intracoastal waters. Occasional lightning strikes are also
possible.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, and lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe harbor
immediately until this storm passes.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued September 15 at 9:32PM AKDT until September 16 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by onshore flow restricting Kuskokwim River
drainage in combination with excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim near Bethel.

* WHEN...Until 700 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
River or stream flows are elevated. Ponding of water in areas is
occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 900 PM AKDT, River gauge reports indicate that receding water
levels have begun to rise again near Bethel, which remains at
minor flood stage. This is due to the Kuskokwim River back-up in
combination with heavy rain across the advisory area. Minor
flooding will continue from overflow of poor drainage areas,
especially along the Kuskokwim.
- Strong onshore winds along the Kuskokwim coast have limited the
ability for the Kuskokwim River to drain out into the Bering Sea.
This has caused rapid river rises along the coast and inland into
Bethel. Water levels are expected to back up along Brown Slough
and flood low lying areas of Bethel and areas along the
Kuskokwim.
- For Kuskokwim River at Bethel:
At 8:51pm the stage was 9.1 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.5 feet.

Impacts:
At 7.0 feet: Action and bankfull stage.
At 8.5 feet: Minor flood stage. Water starts to back up along Brown
Slough and flood low lying areas.
At 12.0 feet: Moderate flood stage.
At 14.0 feet: Major flood stage.


- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

If you live near or along the Kuskokwim River stay alert and be
prepared to take action.

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Levy, Marion and Citrus
Counties.

Horse Creek Near Arcadia at SR 72 affecting DeSoto County.

.Elevated water levels are expected along a few rivers across the
area over the next several days.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Horse Creek near Arcadia at SR 72.

* WHEN...From Thursday evening until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, The access road to Hidden Oak is
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Tuesday the stage was 9.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
Thursday evening and continue rising to a crest of 12.1 feet
early Friday morning.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.1
feet on 09/30/2003.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at 200 PM EDT.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Levy, Marion and Citrus

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

stage at 28.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 06/29/2003.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued September 15 at 8:10PM CDT until September 16 at 3:30PM CDT by NWS Des Moines IA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall
continues.

* WHERE...Adair County in southwestern Iowa...

* WHEN...Until 330 PM CDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 807 PM CDT, Emergency management reported numerous closed
roads in the warned area, with water nearing Highway 25 south of
Greenfield. Flooding is already occurring. Between 2 and 4 inches
of rain have fallen.
- An additional 1 inch or more is possible in the warned area
through the overnight hours. Impacted streams include the Middle
River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Greenfield, Stuart, Adair, Fontanelle, Orient, Bridgewater,
Greenfield Municipal Airport and Nodaway Park.
- This includes Interstate 80 between mile markers 73 and 96.
properties.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

For the latest stream observations and forecasts refer to
weather.gov/desmoines/water.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued September 15 at 4:11PM CDT until September 17 at 4:00AM CDT by NWS Omaha/Valley NE
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Omaha/Valley has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Iowa...

East Nishnabotna River At Red Oak affecting Montgomery County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...East Nishnabotna River at Red Oak.

* WHEN...Until late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Lowland flooding begins along the west
bank.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:00 PM CDT Tuesday the stage was 17.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this afternoon to a crest of 19.7 feet just after midnight
tonight. It will then fall below flood stage by late tomorrow
morning.
- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 19.6
feet on 06/15/1980.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at water.noaa.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at 100 PM CDT.
